   355	  Let \(K\) be an algebraically closed field, let \(A\) be a monoid scheme over \(K\) which
   356	  is proper and geometrically integral over \(K\), and let \(B\) be a group scheme over
   357	  \(K\) which is separated and locally of finite type over \(K\). Then every morphism
   358	  \(g : A \to B\) over \(K\) with \(g \circ e_A = e_B\) is a homomorphism of monoid schemes.
   359	\end{corollary}
   360	\begin{proof}
   361	  \leanok
   362	  \uses{thm:rigidity, lem:product_integral}
   363	  Form the \emph{defect} of \(g\), computed in the group of morphisms
   364	  \(A \times_K A \to B\):
   365	  \[
   366	    \varphi \;=\; \bigl(g \circ \mu_A\bigr) \cdot
   367	      \Bigl(\bigl(g \circ \mathrm{pr}_1\bigr) \cdot \bigl(g \circ \mathrm{pr}_2\bigr)\Bigr)^{-1}.
   368	  \]
   369	  It suffices to prove \(\varphi = 1\) (the constant morphism \(e_B \circ t_{A \times A}\)):
   370	  this says exactly \(g \circ \mu_A = (g \circ \mathrm{pr}_1) \cdot (g \circ \mathrm{pr}_2)
   371	  = \mu_B \circ (g \times g)\), and \(g\) preserves units by hypothesis.
   372	
   373	  \emph{The slice over \(e_A\) collapses.} Precomposition with the slice embedding
   374	  \(\sigma_{e_A} : A \to A \times_K A\) is a group homomorphism, so
   375	  \(\varphi \circ \sigma_{e_A} = (g \circ \mu_A \circ \sigma_{e_A}) \cdot
   376	  \bigl((g \circ \mathrm{pr}_1 \circ \sigma_{e_A}) \cdot
   377	  (g \circ \mathrm{pr}_2 \circ \sigma_{e_A})\bigr)^{-1}\). The right unit law of the monoid
   378	  \(A\) gives \(\mu_A \circ \sigma_{e_A} = \mathrm{id}_A\); moreover
   379	  \(\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ \sigma_{e_A} = \mathrm{id}_A\) and
   380	  \(\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ \sigma_{e_A} = e_A \circ t_A\), so, using
   381	  \(g \circ e_A = e_B\),
   382	  \[
   383	    \varphi \circ \sigma_{e_A}
   384	      \;=\; g \cdot \bigl(g \cdot (e_B \circ t_A)\bigr)^{-1}
   385	      \;=\; g \cdot g^{-1}
   386	      \;=\; 1
   387	      \;=\; e_B \circ t_A .
   388	  \]
   389	
   390	  \emph{Rigidity applies.} In Theorem~\ref{thm:rigidity} take \(X = Y = A\), \(Z = B\),
   391	  \(f = \varphi\), \(y_0 = e_A\), \(z_0 = e_B\): the scheme \(A\) is proper (hence of finite
   392	  type) and geometrically integral over \(K\), so the product \(A \times_K A\) is integral by
   393	  \ref{lem:product_integral}; and \(B\) is separated and locally of finite type. The
   394	  displayed identity is the contraction hypothesis, so there is a (unique) morphism
   395	  \(\psi : A \to B\) with \(\varphi = \psi \circ \mathrm{pr}_2\).
   396	
   397	  \emph{The other slice identifies the factor.} Precompose with
   398	  \(\tau_{e_A} = (e_A \circ t_A, \mathrm{id}_A) : A \to A \times_K A\). Since
   399	  \(\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ \tau_{e_A} = \mathrm{id}_A\), we get
   400	  \(\psi = \varphi \circ \tau_{e_A}\). Computing as before, with the left unit law
   401	  \(\mu_A \circ \tau_{e_A} = \mathrm{id}_A\), and
   402	  \(\mathrm{pr}_1 \circ \tau_{e_A} = e_A \circ t_A\),
   403	  \(\mathrm{pr}_2 \circ \tau_{e_A} = \mathrm{id}_A\):
   404	  \[
   405	    \psi \;=\; g \cdot \bigl((e_B \circ t_A) \cdot g\bigr)^{-1}
   406	        \;=\; g \cdot g^{-1} \;=\; 1 .
   407	  \]
   408	  Hence \(\varphi = 1 \circ \mathrm{pr}_2 = 1\), as required.
   409	\end{proof}
